findings.detail: Both baseline and first current choices put conditional future policy/requirement formalization under necessary_handoffs even though the requested draft can end with unresolved facts. Ownership/output and absence of actual scope expansion still pass. Root rejects the necessary-handoff facet, not the entire produced artifact.

Baseline starts with an unrequested requirement-author stage; current prioritizes orchestration solely from cross-service scope even though the immediate missing semantic/compatibility decision has an architecture owner. Both correctly block implementation. Root grades the immediate owner as a misroute in both versions and the requirement-artifact handoff as unnecessary.

Both versions declare a future slice-implementer handoff as necessary for a diagnosis-only request, before the causal finding identifies the repair unit. That conditional future choice is premature; diagnosis remains the correct immediate owner.
